title: Join paths safely
description:
A mod asks for files by relative path. Write `safeJoin(base, relative)`, which returns `base` joined with `relative`, or `std::nullopt` if the request could reach outside `base`. Paths use `\` or `/` as separators; the result uses `\`.

Reject (return `std::nullopt`) if `relative`:

- is empty;
- is absolute: starts with `\` or `/`, or has a drive letter (`C:`), or contains `:` anywhere (which on Windows also names alternate data streams);
- contains any component that is `..`;
- contains an empty component (two separators in a row such as `a//b`, or a trailing separator), or a component that ends with a space or a dot (Windows silently strips those, so `secret.txt.` would open `secret.txt`), except the component `.` itself, which is simply skipped.

Otherwise return `base`, a single `\`, and the components joined with `\` (skipping `.` components). If only `.` components remain, return `base` unchanged.

```
safeJoin("C:\Game\mods\lantern", "textures/light.png")  ->  "C:\Game\mods\lantern\textures\light.png"
safeJoin("C:\Game\mods\lantern", "../../saves/a.sav")   ->  nullopt
```
hints: Reject the easy cases first: empty, starting with a separator, or containing `:` anywhere.
Split on both separators. For each component: an empty one (two separators in a row) is refused; `.` is skipped; `..` is refused; one ending in a space or a dot is refused; anything else is kept.
lessonTitle: Secure Coding: Buffers, Integers and Trust
